title: Don't crucify me. Want to learn how to make game
author: adolphite
selftext: Does anyone have any video that I can check out to help create the map or level design of a top down 2D game? I want to know how I can bring the concept of a building, roads, npc etc into the game?

comments.author: adolphite
comments.body: When I use the AI it feels like the building has been painted or perhaps some cardboxes. Surely there must be a better way because none of the games I have played in the past look like that. When I even tried to add some sway to the leaves on the trees, the leaves move with the side of the building right behind it. If I can know how to create the map, I think I can then tell the AI how to do it and do it right. Right now I don't even know the terminology to use

replies.author: SolGuy
replies.body:
Have you done any game development in engines like Godot? If not may I suggest watching some tutorials. Don't worry about programming if you are not too familiar. Watch how people build and the tools they use. Learn what it means to place a character and give them animations and how to build an interactive world. Learn game design and not tgame development. Get familiar with the concepts and try again.

I am building my game in Godot but I don't use an MCP, the AI builds the scenes and scripts and runs it. Play around with asking simple stuff, practice. Don't worry about the final product yet. You need experience first.

replies.author: adolphite
replies.body: I have used Gadot to build a game that is common among the locals here. There's a part where a hand has to pick and distribute seeds. I know exactly what I want. I want to take away the hand the AI built and use a hand drawn hand to pick the seeds. I want the seed picking and distributing to have an animation. I find that this is the thing missing in my game development. I don't want the Ai to just do it for me as I want to know how to do it and then use the AI better

comments.author: adolphite
comments.body: Can you describe the way you do it?

comments.author: adolphite
comments.body: This is what I am looking for. I didn't know what to search. Thank you

comments.author: adolphite
comments.body: Was the image in your game generated in code? I don't want it that way..maybe I am not using the right terminology. I want to get for e.g an NPC in various poses and use that frame of poses to get generate an animation in the game. The same with the protagonist. Does it make sense? Then the map itself. There's a small harbor as part of the town that I want to build. Can I buy images or even use AI to generate those image and then load it into Godot and let the AI use those image in the game? How? Does the image need to be prepared into a certain style before importation?

replies.author: ReceptionLanky3374
replies.body:
It was generated with GenAI (ChatGPT), search up Spritesheets, thats how you animate 2d characters. You can make all kinds of things with spritesheets including destructable buildings, attacking tanks.. whatever you can imagine  
Just tell it that you need one for a 2d isometric game, and let the AI take care of the camera & render settings in Godot.   
The AI will take care of all preperations, you dont need to worry about it.

comments.author: Claude_human_4271
comments.body: Not sure what you ask for, people have suggested tools but I also suggest you look at GDC videos on game design and maybe read some 80.lv articles

replies.author: ReceptionLanky3374
replies.body:
Bc ChatGPT has GenAI, if you truly want a 2d game, not a 2.5d, you can generate all the images easily with it.   
This is a short game that I made for fun, every single image you see was made with ChatGPT: [https://www.spawn.co/@faryanh/sektor-null](https://www.spawn.co/@faryanh/sektor-null)

comments.author: shaymagen
comments.body: look up tilemaps, that's how almost every top down 2d game does buildings and roads. Tiled is a free map editor where you paint the level with tiles and load it into godot/phaser/unity, and npcs are just objects you drop on a separate layer. any "tiled + <your engine>" tutorial on youtube will get you going fast
